ground.decision: A continuous cold snow mantle accumulates in hollows and covers shallow rocky paint. Use rougher packed firn at the existing service areas and fractured rock only where a steep face actually sheds snow.
ground.reject: Do not import a muddy field, tire ruts or a permanent blue tint. Preserve shallow grain, genuine shade and the difference between open snow and exposed rock.

foliage.decision: Retain the treeless and shrubless glacial battlefield. Mounted outcrops, equipment and bones are not vegetation.
foliage.reject: No evergreen belt, dead tree scatter or tuft quota. Dry exposed stone does not indicate tundra planting.

review.basis: The Hoth exterior and exposed polar ice views show bare snow and rock without woody cover; the mounted starting inventory contains only rocks, equipment and bones. This is the surveyed board, not a claim about all polar terrain.

exclude.where: Entire playable snowfield and its glacier-ridge surroundings.
exclude.reason: Open polar snow, stone and working surfaces remain visible to the horizon.

variation.decision: Keep variation in snow, striation and outcrop shapes, not vegetation types.
limits: Allocate no grass, shrub, tree or scenic crown layers.

landmark.decision: Keep the mounted ion cannon, cargo, pipes, skeleton and rocks at their authored roots. Existing large structures should read across the clearing.
landmark.reject: Do not reconstruct Echo Base or add trench networks, vehicles or a station building from reference photographs.

natural.decision: Continuous snow covers flats, with relatively blue shade, wind-lined depressions, and darker rock exposures allowed on steep faces.

built.decision: Retain building geometry and its silhouette. Only actual construction can license a concrete footing. No photographed polar building grants permission to pave a mount.

transition.decision: The exterior working court remains packed snow up to the equipment feet. Restore rougher snow where traffic ends; keep the boundary at actual structures.

outskirts.skyline: A low open snow basin leads to irregular overlapping ridges, glacial shoulders and passes. Snow accumulates on shallow slopes between exposed faces.
outskirts.join: Continue the exact snowy perimeter and normal field into the mountain basin. The exterior is renderer-only and has no collision, scripts, fog reveal or artificial planting.
outskirts.reject: No smooth cone wall, planted rim or flat tabletop against the sky.

climate.substrate: A single mineral-poor snowfield links the muster and rib basins; roughness and grain may vary without painting alternating hues into the ice.
climate.lighting: Use the real Hoth skies and SNOW_RANDOM schedule. Compare snow on both sides of each basin, including the natural clear interval. Blue shadow and warm direct sunlight are light, not dyed snow.
climate.exceptions: Keep hard rock silhouettes, shadow beneath equipment and compacted firn in yards. Warm or blue light can change value and chroma; do not white-balance it away.

pairs.basis: Two open snow windows beyond the deployed eastern infantry. Both exclude units, the service props, the HUD and the near rock face.
Visible snow mass on either side of the rib basin, above the mounted bones and away from the dark exposed faces.

uncertain: Polar field photographs are analogues for the shape of snow, escarpments and service access, not fictional architecture or exact snow colour. The original map dictates base and equipment positions.
